spec: A robot starts at position (0, 0) facing north ("N") on an infinite grid. commands is a list of single characters: "L" turns the robot 90 degrees counter-clockwise in place, "R" turns it 90 degrees clockwise in place, and "F" moves it one grid unit forward in the direction it currently faces (north increases y, south decreases y, east increases x, west decreases x). Return a tuple (x, y, facing) giving the robot's final position and facing direction (one of "N", "S", "E", "W") after processing all commands in order.

A vending machine tracks inserted credit. events is a list of (op, value) tuples: ("insert", amount) adds amount to the current credit, and ("select", price) dispenses an item and subtracts price from the credit only if the current credit is greater than or equal to price; otherwise the selection is ignored and credit is unchanged. Return a tuple (final_credit, items_dispensed) where items_dispensed counts how many selections succeeded.

A parking lot has room for capacity cars. events is a list of (op, spot_id) tuples: ("enter", spot_id) parks a car in spot_id, but is ignored if the lot is already full (capacity cars parked) or spot_id is already occupied; ("exit", spot_id) removes the car from spot_id, or does nothing if that spot was not occupied. Return a sorted list of the spot_ids that are occupied after processing all events.

Tally a game score from events, a list where each item is ("score", pts) to add pts to the score, ("bonus",) to double the current score, or ("penalty", pts) to subtract pts from the score, clamped so the score never goes below 0. Start the score at 0 and return the final score after applying all events in order.

A thermostat has a target temperature, starting at initial_target, and a mode that starts as "IDLE". events is a list of (op, value) tuples: ("set_target", temp) changes the target temperature without changing the mode; ("read", current_temp) updates the mode based on comparing current_temp to the current target: mode becomes "HEAT" if current_temp is less than target, "COOL" if current_temp is greater than target, and "IDLE" if they are equal. Return the mode after processing all events in order.

Track library book checkouts. events is a list of (op, book) tuples: ("checkout", book) marks book as checked out, unless it is already checked out, in which case the event is ignored; ("return", book) marks book as available again, or does nothing if it was not checked out. Return a sorted list of the books that are currently checked out after processing all events.

A washing machine state machine starts in state "OFF" and has states "OFF", "RUNNING", and "PAUSED". events is a list of strings, each one of "start", "pause", "resume", or "stop". "start" moves the machine from OFF to RUNNING (ignored otherwise); "pause" moves it from RUNNING to PAUSED (ignored otherwise); "resume" moves it from PAUSED to RUNNING (ignored otherwise); "stop" moves it from RUNNING or PAUSED back to OFF (ignored if already OFF). Any event that is not a valid transition from the current state is ignored. Return the final state after processing all events in order.

timestamps is a non-decreasing list of integers giving the arrival times of requests, in the order received. limit and window are positive integers. A request arriving at time t is allowed if the total number of requests (counting itself and every earlier request in the list, regardless of whether those were allowed) with a timestamp in the half-open-from-below range (t - window, t] is at most limit. Return a list of booleans, one per timestamp, in the same order as timestamps, indicating whether each request was allowed.

A door has three states, "LOCKED", "CLOSED", and "OPEN", starting at "CLOSED". events is a list of strings, each one of "lock", "unlock", "open", or "close". "lock" moves CLOSED to LOCKED; "unlock" moves LOCKED to CLOSED; "open" moves CLOSED to OPEN; "close" moves OPEN to CLOSED. Every event that does not match one of these exact transitions from the current state is ignored. Return the final state after processing all events in order.

Track scores for two players from events, a list of (player, pts) tuples where player is "P1" or "P2" and pts is an int that may be negative. Add pts to that player's running score, but never let a player's score go below 0 (clamp at 0). Both scores start at 0. Return a tuple (p1_score, p2_score) after processing all events in order.

A traffic light cycles forever through RED, then GREEN, then YELLOW, then back to RED, where durations is a tuple (red_ticks, green_ticks, yellow_ticks) giving how many ticks each phase lasts, and the light is RED at tick 0. Given n_ticks (a non-negative integer), return a list of length n_ticks giving the light's state (one of "RED", "GREEN", "YELLOW") at ticks 0, 1, ..., n_ticks - 1 in order.

Track balances across several named bank accounts. events is a list where each item is ("deposit", acct, amt), ("withdraw", acct, amt), or ("transfer", from_acct, to_acct, amt), with amt a non-negative number. Any account is created with balance 0 the first time it is referenced by any event. A deposit adds amt to acct's balance. A withdrawal subtracts amt from acct's balance only if the balance is at least amt, otherwise it is ignored. A transfer moves amt from from_acct to to_acct only if from_acct's balance is at least amt, otherwise the whole transfer is ignored. Return a dict mapping every account name that was referenced to its final balance.

An elevator starts at start_floor and must visit each floor in requests (a list of ints) in the given order, one after another, without any optimization or reordering. Return the total distance traveled, computed as the sum of the absolute differences between consecutive floors visited (starting from start_floor).

A four-way intersection alternates between a phase where the north-south (N/S) direction has a green light and a phase where the east-west (E/W) direction has a green light, each phase lasting green_duration ticks, starting with the N/S phase at tick 0. events is a list of (tick, direction) tuples where direction is one of "N", "S", "E", "W", meaning a car in that direction arrives at that tick. A car passes through only if its direction's light is green at that tick. Return the total number of cars that passed.

A counter starts at 0 and is bounded between 0 and cap (inclusive). events is a list of strings, each one of "inc" (increase the counter by 1, unless it is already at cap, in which case it stays), "dec" (decrease the counter by 1, unless it is already at 0, in which case it stays), or "reset" (set the counter back to 0). Return the final counter value after processing all events in order.

An elevator starts at floor min_floor with its door "CLOSED". commands is a list of strings: "open" sets the door to "OPEN", "close" sets the door to "CLOSED", and "up"/"down" move the elevator one floor up or down (bounded within [min_floor, max_floor]) but only take effect while the door is CLOSED; while the door is OPEN, "up" and "down" commands are ignored. Return a tuple (final_floor, final_door_state) after processing all commands in order.

Simulate a shopping cart. events is a list where each item is ("add", item, qty, price) which adds qty units of item to the cart at the given unit price (updating the stored price and adding to any existing quantity of that item), ("remove", item, qty) which reduces the quantity of item by qty (removing the item entirely from the cart if the resulting quantity would be zero or less; removing an item not in the cart does nothing), or ("clear",) which empties the cart. Return the total cost of everything currently in the cart, computed as the sum over items of quantity times unit price.

A turnstile starts LOCKED. events is a list of strings, each "coin" or "push". A "coin" event sets the state to UNLOCKED. A "push" event, only when the state is UNLOCKED, locks the turnstile again and counts as one successful pass; a push while LOCKED has no effect. Return a tuple (final_state, pass_count) after processing all events in order.

A robot vacuum starts at (0, 0) facing north ("N") on a grid, and obstacles is a list of (x, y) coordinate tuples it cannot enter. commands is a list of single characters: "L" turns the robot 90 degrees counter-clockwise in place, "R" turns it 90 degrees clockwise in place, and "F" moves it one unit forward in its current facing direction unless the destination cell is in obstacles, in which case the robot stays where it is. Every cell the robot occupies (including its starting cell) counts as cleaned. Return the number of distinct cells cleaned after processing all commands.

A parking garage charges by time. events is a list of (op, car_id, time) tuples where op is "enter" or "exit" and time is a non-negative integer. An "enter" records the car's arrival time, unless that car is already parked, in which case it is ignored. An "exit" for a car that is currently parked computes a fee of (exit_time - enter_time) * rate and removes the car from the parked set; an "exit" for a car that is not currently parked is ignored. Return a dict mapping each car_id that successfully exited to its computed fee.

A traffic light for cars cycles forever: RED for red_duration ticks then GREEN for green_duration ticks, starting RED at tick 0. Pedestrians can only cross while the car light is RED. arrivals is a list of non-negative integers giving the tick at which each pedestrian arrives, in the order they arrive. Each pedestrian crosses at the first tick that is greater than or equal to their arrival time and during which the car light is RED. Return a list of the crossing ticks, one per pedestrian, in the same order as arrivals.

Simulate a simple undo/redo document. commands is a list where each item is ("do", value) which appends value to the end of the document and clears any pending redo history, ("undo",) which removes the last value in the document (moving it to the redo history), doing nothing if the document is empty, or ("redo",) which re-appends the most recently undone value from the redo history, doing nothing if there is no such value. Return the final document as a list, in order, after processing all commands.

A voting gate starts CLOSED. events is a list of strings, each "yes" or "no", and threshold is a positive integer. Maintain a running net score that increases by 1 for each "yes" and decreases by 1 for each "no". As soon as the net score reaches threshold or higher, the gate becomes OPEN and stays OPEN permanently, ignoring all further events. Return the final gate state as the string "OPEN" or "CLOSED".

A coffee machine has a dict prices mapping drink name to price and a dict stock mapping drink name to units remaining. events is a list of (op, value) tuples: ("insert", amount) adds amount to the current credit, and ("select", drink) dispenses one unit of drink, subtracting its price from the credit and its count from stock, but only if drink has stock remaining greater than 0 and the current credit is at least its price; otherwise the selection is ignored and nothing changes. Return a tuple (final_credit, final_stock, total_dispensed) where final_stock is the stock dict after all dispenses and total_dispensed counts successful selections. The input stock dict must not be modified.

A bank account starts at balance 0. events is a list of (op, amount) tuples where op is "deposit" or "withdraw". A deposit adds amount to the balance. A withdrawal removes amount plus a flat fee from the balance, but only if the balance is at least amount + fee; otherwise the withdrawal (and its fee) is skipped entirely and the balance is unchanged. Return the final balance after processing all events in order.

An elevator starts at start_floor and sweeps one floor at a time in the given direction (1 for up, -1 for down), stopping only at floors that appear in requests (a list of ints), until it reaches floor 1 (if going down) or top_floor (if going up), at which point the sweep ends after checking that final floor too. Return a list of the floors stopped at, in the order they are visited.

A robot starts at (0, 0) with a given amount of fuel. commands is a list of single characters, each "N", "S", "E", or "W", meaning move one unit in that direction. Each successful move consumes 1 unit of fuel; once fuel reaches 0, no further moves happen (remaining commands are ignored, though fuel never goes negative). Return a tuple ((x, y), remaining_fuel) giving the final position and remaining fuel after processing all commands in order.

Simulate a retail checkout register. events is a list where each item is ("scan", price) which adds price to the current transaction, ("void",) which removes the most recently scanned item from the current transaction (doing nothing if the transaction is empty), or ("pay",) which finalizes the current transaction, recording its total (the sum of its remaining scanned prices), and starts a new empty transaction. Any items scanned after the last "pay" event with no following "pay" are not included in any total. Return a list of the finalized transaction totals, in the order the "pay" events occurred.

There are n lights in a row, indexed 0 to n-1, all starting off. events is a list where each item is ("toggle", i) which flips light i between on and off, ("toggle_all",) which flips every light, or ("reset",) which turns every light off. Return the final list of n booleans (True for on, False for off) after processing all events in order.

Simulate a waiting line with a server that can handle several people at once. events is a list where each item is ("arrive", person_id) which adds person_id to the back of the queue, or ("serve",) which removes up to capacity people from the front of the queue (fewer if the queue has fewer than capacity people waiting). Return the final queue contents as a list, ordered from front to back, after processing all events in order.

Track a loan balance. events is a list of (op, amount) tuples where op is "borrow" or "repay" and amount is a non-negative number. A borrow increases the debt by amount without limit. A repay decreases the debt by amount, but the debt can never go below 0: if amount exceeds the current debt, the debt simply becomes 0 and the excess is not carried over or refunded. Return the final debt after processing all events in order.

Two independent traffic lights each cycle forever through RED, then GREEN, then YELLOW, then back to RED, starting RED at tick 0; durations_a and durations_b are each a tuple (red_ticks, green_ticks, yellow_ticks) giving the two lights' own phase durations. Given n_ticks (a non-negative integer), count how many ticks t in range 0 to n_ticks - 1 (inclusive of 0, exclusive of n_ticks) have both lights showing GREEN at the same time. Return that count.
